The first consideration is that the expiration of the period of limitation prescribed for making an appeal gives rise to a right in favour of the State Represented By vs Tr.M.Selvamoorthy on 27 August, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146017733/
10 decree-holder to treat the decree as binding beteween the parties.

In other words,
when the period of limitation prescribed has expired, the decree-holder has obtained a benefit under the law of limitation to treat the decree as beyond challenge, and this legal right which has accrued to the decree-holder by lapse of time should not be light heartedly disturbed.
The other consideration which cannot be ignored is that if sufficient cause for excusing delay is shown, discretion is given to the court to condone delay and admit the appeal.
